tickets.title: Comments API: investigate custom comment composer flow after pending comment creation
tickets.description:
## Context and problem statement

A customer implementing a custom comment composer reported problems integrating with the built-in floating comment bubble flow.

When the user clicks the floating comment bubble:

* SuperDoc inserts a pending comment mark
* The live selection is destroyed/mutated
* Integrations lose access to stable selection state
* Positional data is not exposed back to the integrator

Customer quote:

> "Pending comment flow requires workarounds."

## Current workaround

The customer currently:

* Continuously snapshots selection state into a ref
* Captures selection preemptively
* Defers `createFromCapture()` by one animation frame
* Manually avoids transaction timing conflicts

Example supported flow today:

```ts
const capture = ui.selection.capture();
ui.comments.createFromCapture(capture, { text });
```

## Investigation goals

Need more information from the customer about:

* Intended custom composer UX
* What interaction/state should survive after clicking the floating comment bubble
* Whether selection restoration is required
* Whether positional anchoring is the primary issue
* Whether lifecycle timing hooks would solve the problem

Need to determine whether the missing capability is:

* Selection preservation
* Pending-comment lifecycle events
* Pre-mutation callbacks
* Pending-comment recovery APIs
* Broader comment composer extensibility

## Potential follow-up directions

Possible future APIs may include:

* `createFromPending()`
* Pre-mutation callback
* Pending-comment lifecycle events
* Selection preservation helpers

These are exploratory only at this stage.

## Context

Current integrations require animation-frame timing workarounds, continuous selection snapshots, and manual transaction conflict avoidance. This creates fragile integration behavior for advanced custom comment experiences.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Gather additional customer UX details
* Reproduce current lifecycle behavior
* Determine where selection state is lost
* Identify whether API gaps or internal lifecycle behavior are responsible
* Determine appropriate long-term API direction

tickets.title: Layout API: investigate responsive fit-to-container and layout event gaps
tickets.description:
## Context and problem statement

A customer implementing responsive editor layouts reported several gaps around fit-to-container behavior and layout synchronization.

Current customer implementation manually measures page width, recalculates zoom on resize, polls for layout shifts, and detects comments rail appearance/disappearance manually.

Customer quote:

> "No responsive fit-to-container."

## Current supported APIs

Current zoom API:

```ts
superdoc.setZoom(150);

superdoc.on('zoomChange', ({ zoom }) => {
  // ...
});
```

The customer also relies on undocumented `responsiveToContainer: true` for toolbar sizing behavior.

## Reported issues

* `setZoom()` scales the page but not the comments rail
* Internal layout changes emit no dedicated events
* Rail appearance/disappearance is difficult to detect
* Integrations must continuously measure layout state
* Polling is required to detect certain layout invalidations

## Investigation goals

Need deeper investigation into:

* Fit-to-container expectations
* Comments rail interactions
* Layout invalidation events
* Resize/layout synchronization
* Current undocumented `responsiveToContainer` behavior

Need to determine whether this should become:

* A formal fit-to-container mode
* A dedicated layout event system
* Comments rail lifecycle events
* Broader layout architecture improvements

## Context

Current integrations require polling, manual measurements, resize observers, and undocumented configuration. This creates maintenance burden and fragile responsive behavior.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Engineering understands the specific missing layout signals
* Determine whether existing APIs are insufficient vs buggy
* Determine whether fit-to-container should become a first-class capability
* Determine what layout events should exist publicly

tickets.title: Feature: Viewport API expose public editor scroll container access
tickets.description:
## Context and problem statement

A customer integrating advanced custom UI behavior needs access to the editor scroll container. Today there is no public API or lifecycle event for obtaining the internal scroll element.

The customer currently uses a `MutationObserver` to wait for `.super-editor-container` to appear asynchronously in the DOM:

```ts
const observer = new MutationObserver(...);
```

or:

```ts
superdoc.once('ready', () => {
  const scrollEl = superdoc.element?.querySelector('.super-editor-container');
});
```

This depends on internal DOM structure, internal class names, and asynchronous mount timing—making integrations fragile and prone to breakage on upgrades.

## Requested outcome

Provide stable public API access to the editor scroll container without requiring DOM polling or reliance on internal selectors.

Potential solutions:

* `ui.viewport.getScrollContainer()`
* Public lifecycle event when viewport mounts
* Documented stable selector contract
* Supported viewport container access pattern

## Scope

* Obtaining the editor scroll container element after initialization
* Reliable access without MutationObserver polling
* Stable API that survives internal DOM/layout refactors

## Out of scope

None specified

## Visuals

None provided

## Context

Without a stable public API:

* Integrations rely on undocumented DOM structure
* Integrations require MutationObservers
* Upgrades risk breaking integrations
* Custom viewport behavior becomes fragile

## Acceptance Criteria

* Integrations can obtain the editor scroll container without DOM polling
* No MutationObserver required
* No reliance on `.super-editor-container`
* API works reliably after initialization
* API remains stable across internal DOM/layout refactors

tickets.title: Feature: Viewport API formal overlay / annotation layer support
tickets.description:
## Context and problem statement

A customer is building non-persisted visual overlays anchored to document locations. There is currently no formal overlay or annotation layer API for rendering custom HTML aligned with document positions.

The customer built a workaround system using `coordsAtPos`, undocumented internal `positionTracker`, `ResizeObserver`, scroll listeners, and a 500ms polling sentinel for layout shifts.

Customer quote:

> "No document overlay/annotation layer. No API to render custom HTML positioned at document locations (non-persisted visual overlays)."

While existing supported pieces include `ui.viewport.getHost()` and `ui.viewport.getRect()`, these APIs are not sufficient for stable overlay lifecycle management.

## Requested outcome

A formal overlay layer API that:

* Anchors UI to document entities/ranges
* Updates reliably during layout changes
* Supports viewport-relative positioning
* Avoids polling
* Avoids undocumented internal APIs

## Scope

Customer use cases include:

* Inline annotations
* Contextual widgets
* AI affordances
* Transient visual markers
* Document-linked UI
* Non-persisted interaction layers

## Out of scope

None specified

## Visuals

None provided

## Context

Current workaround implementation requires polling, layout heuristics, undocumented APIs, and manual synchronization during resize/zoom/layout shifts. This is fragile and difficult to maintain.

## Acceptance Criteria

* Overlays can be mounted declaratively against document targets
* Layout changes trigger reliable updates
* No polling loop required
* No undocumented APIs required
* Overlay positioning survives zoom/resize/scroll/layout changes

tickets.title: Bug: Comments API activation flicker during comment scrolling
tickets.description:
## Expected outcome

Calling `ui.comments.scrollTo(commentId)` should smoothly scroll to and activate the target comment without any visual flickering of the highlight state.

## Steps to reproduce

\[Environment: Customer integration with custom comments UI\]

1. Call `ui.comments.scrollTo(commentId)` to scroll to a comment
2. Observe the target comment highlight during the scroll animation
3. Observed result: The active comment highlight rapidly toggles between dark-pink (active) and light-pink (inactive) states multiple times during the animated scroll

## Type of issue

API / Interaction

## Visuals

None provided

## Context

A customer integrating a custom comments UI reported that `ui.comments.scrollTo(commentId)` causes the target comment highlight to rapidly toggle between active and inactive states during smooth scrolling.

Customer quote:

> "ui.comments.scrollTo() causes the comment highlight to rapidly toggle between active (dark pink) and inactive (light pink) during the scroll animation."

This creates visible UI instability in custom comment experiences and makes comment synchronization feel unreliable.

The customer also requested a stable activation-only API such as `await ui.comments.setActive(commentId)`. This may become a follow-up feature request depending on investigation findings.

**Investigation goals:**

* Determine whether the flicker is caused by scroll animation behavior, repeated activation/deactivation during viewport updates, comment visibility synchronization, selection state updates, consumer-side timing/state handling, or another internal comment lifecycle issue
* Determine whether fix belongs in existing `scrollTo()`, a new activate-only API, or internal comment activation behavior

## Acceptance Criteria

* Engineering can reliably reproduce the flicker
* Root cause is identified
* Determine appropriate fix location (scrollTo, new API, or internal behavior)
